items.q: What is the Assistant?
items.a: It is the part of the Studio where you describe what you need and it builds a team, an agent or a workflow for you. It asks questions, shows a plan, and builds a draft you review and save. You can still build everything by hand.

items.q: Do I need to know how to code?
items.a: No. You describe what you need to the Assistant, or you build in the Studio with names, plain-word descriptions and drag and drop. Two things do need a technical colleague: installing the Community edition on a server, and building a VibeApp of your own.

items.q: Which AI model does it use?
items.a: The one you choose: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI or AWS Bedrock. You can change it later.

items.q: Where does my data go?
items.a: With the Community edition, nothing leaves your server unless you connect a service. When an AI step runs, what you send in that step goes to the model provider you chose, under its terms.

items.q: Does it replace my team?
items.a: No. It takes the repetitive work and comes back to your people for the decisions. The judgment stays with those who know the job.

cta.sub: Join the waitlist and be first on the cloud.
cta.fine: No spam. First access when the cloud launches.

meta.description: The free Community edition of Agentivity runs on your own machine or server with Docker. One command to start, the Studio included.

hero.sub: The Community edition is for people who are comfortable with Docker. One command starts Agentivity on your machine or your server, with the Studio included.
hero.hub: See the image on Docker Hub
hero.not_technical: Not technical? The cloud version needs no installation.

steps.title: Get Docker
steps.body: Docker Desktop on Windows or macOS, Docker Engine on Linux.

steps.title: Start Agentivity
steps.body: One command. Your data is kept in a Docker volume, so it survives a restart or an update.

steps.title: Open the Studio
steps.body: In your browser, on the machine where it runs:

steps.title: Connect an AI model
steps.body: Add the key of the provider you use: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI or AWS Bedrock. Then create your first agent and run it.

items.title: There is no login yet
items.body: Anyone who can reach the server can use it. Keep it on a network you trust, or behind your own access control. Never expose it directly to the internet.

items.title: Your data stays with you
items.body: Agents, teams, workflows, tables and settings are stored in the agentivity-data volume. Back it up like any other data. What you send in an AI step goes to the model provider you chose.

items.title: Updating
items.body: Pull the new image, remove the container and start it again with the same command. The volume keeps your data.
items.command: docker pull agentivitylabs/agentivity && docker rm -f agentivity

items.title: What is included

items.q: Is the Community edition really free?

items.q: Can I use it for my business?

items.q: I am not technical. Which edition is for me?

items.q: Can I deliver Agentivity under my own brand?

It builds a draft and draws it as it goes

beats: Add a member to a team
Make the instructions clearer and more precise
Add something to what you already have

Your choice: rebuild with some of it, all of it, or none

steps: You save: you see what is added, and choose where it goes
It lands in your workspace like anything you built yourself
Open it in the editor to change it, publish it, run it

points.title: A plan before anything is built
points.body: It shows what it intends to build, in plain words, and waits for your go-ahead.

points.title: A draft, not a change
points.body: Nothing is saved until you save. Until then, nothing in your workspace moves.

points.title: Checked before you save
points.body: It checks what it built. An error stops the save; a warning is for you to weigh.

points.title: Your keys stay yours
points.body: It sees the name of your model connection, never its secrets.

items.title: It drafts, you review.
items.body: A first version is rarely the last. Read the plan, look at the result and try it on a real case, as you would with a new colleague's work.

items.title: It tells you what is missing.
items.body: In the example above it reminded us to provide the competitors' website addresses. That part is yours.

items.title: It corrects itself, in the open.
items.body: When it gets a step wrong, you see it, and you see the fix.

items.title: It uses your AI model.
items.body: It works through the model connection you set up, so what you write goes to that provider, under its terms, and its usage is billed to you by that provider.

items.q: Is the Assistant part of the Community edition?
items.a: Yes. It is in the Studio, in the free Community edition. It needs a connection to an AI model, which you set up once.

items.q: Do I need to know how to code, or what a workflow is?
items.a: No. You describe what you need in your own words, and the Assistant answers in the words of your work, not technical ones.

items.q: Can I use it on something I already built?
items.a: Yes. The Assistant is in the main sidebar and in the agent, team and workflow editors: open one of yours and launch the Assistant to improve it, or start from the Assistant and pick the one to work on. It opens in a new conversation, and nothing changes until you save.

items.q: Does it replace building by hand?
items.a: No. The Studio is unchanged. The Assistant is the fast way to a first version, to a change, or to a second opinion. Anyone who prefers to draw it themselves still can.

items.q: Which AI model does it use?
items.a: The connection you choose: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI or AWS Bedrock. You also choose which model the agents it builds will run on, and you can change it later.

items.q: Is what I write sent to Agentivity?
items.a: No. With the Community edition everything runs on your server. What you write goes only to the AI model provider you connected.

cta.sub: The Community edition is free forever, and the Assistant is part of it.

items.title: The conversation, and the team
items.body: A person picks a solution and writes a request. The conversation is on the left, and the team is drawn on the right.

points.title: People stay in charge
points.body: The team proposes. The app stops and asks each time a choice belongs to the person.

points.title: Change the work, not the app
points.body: The team is built and changed in the Studio, in plain words. The application stays the same.

points.title: Your server and your keys
points.body: The Community edition runs on your own server, with your own key from your AI model provider.

items.q: Do I need a developer?
items.a: Not for the team: it is built in the Studio. The portal is ready-made, and a developer installs it once. An application of your own needs a developer and the SDK.

items.q: Can a VibeApp have classic screens too?
items.a: Yes. A list of past requests, a profile page: most real VibeApps mix ordinary screens and a team.

items.q: Is a classic app sometimes better?
items.a: Yes. When everyone needs the same thing, a form is right.

items.q: What does each request cost?
items.a: Each request uses an AI model, and your provider bills you for it, with your own key.
